html:
I’ve been mulling things over lately, and I’d like to start a series on the giants of acoustics: leading figures in the field whom I know personally or know about. I’m trying a “lightweight” style, so the pieces won’t be long or tiring to read. Tips are very welcome. The sources listed at the end are valuable too, so do take a look if you want to learn more about the field.

Fanyu:

The first installment had to be about my advisor, the Brad Pitt of acoustics. He is gentle and witty, and he reportedly has a whole crowd of adoring fans at the Acoustical Society of America. In 2017 I went to a conference in Hong Kong with Michael and saw academic fandom up close for the first time; I ended up as the stand-in photographer. Michael’s influence is enormous, and when I later went job hunting I benefited from my advisor’s name. He retires this year, but like the other greats of the field, he won’t sit idle: he will stay active in academia.

Er Mu:

“Refined” could have been coined for Michael. He has the poise down to a T; drop him in Hollywood and he would be the one pressing his handprints into the cement. But of course looks aren’t everything. Michael, who has literally written the book and founded a school of thought, is rigorous to the core in his research. I still remember what he said while correcting one of my papers: the description of the experiments and the data in a paper must be good enough for your peers to reproduce! Respect!!!

Education and early career [1, 2]

  • 1978–1981: Studied physics at the University of Dortmund

  • 1981–1984: Studied physics at RWTH Aachen University, earning his physics diploma

  • 1985–1989: Research assistant at the Institute of Technical Acoustics, RWTH Aachen University

  • 1989: Doctorate in natural sciences (Dr. rer. nat.)

  • 1989–1991: Researcher at PTB (Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Germany’s national metrology institute)

  • 1991–1996: Head of the building acoustics laboratory at PTB

  • 1995: Habilitation at TU Dresden

Academic career [1, 3, 4, 5]

  • March 1, 1996 – present: Professor and director of the Institute of Technical Acoustics, RWTH Aachen University

  • 2004–2007: President of the European Acoustics Association (EAA)

  • 2007–2010: Vice president of the European Acoustics Association (EAA)

  • 2011–2013: President of the International Commission for Acoustics (ICA)

  • 2016–2019: President of the German Acoustical Society (DEGA)

  • 2024–2027: President of the Acoustical Society of America (ASA), from president-elect through past president

Research contributions [6, 7, 8]

Professor Vorländer has published more than 300 scholarly papers. His 2008 monograph Auralization is widely regarded as the founding work of the field.

Major honors [9, 10, 11]

  • 2005: R. W. B. Stephens Medal, Institute of Acoustics (UK)

  • 2006: Elected Fellow of the Acoustical Society of America (ASA)

  • 2014: EAA Award, European Acoustics Association

  • 2018: Wallace Clement Sabine Medal, Acoustical Society of America

  • 2021: Medal of the Czech Technical University in Prague, first class

  • 2021: Rayleigh Medal, Institute of Acoustics (UK)

Coming next: Heinrich Kuttruff
